title: Bonucci targets Juventus head coach role in the future
subtitle: Juventus travel to Lecce on Sunday, with the Bianconeri hoping to reduce the pressure on Luciano Spalletti with a win in Serie A.
paragraphs: Former Juventus defender Leonardo Bonucci revealed his dream role is to become head coach of either Italy or the Bianconeri.
Bonucci made 502 appearances for Juve across two spells, which were split by a brief one-season stint with rivals AC Milan.
The centre-back won eight Serie A titles with Juve and four Coppa Italia titles, while also helping them reach the Champions League final twice, losing on both occasions.
Bonucci is currently a part of Roberto Mancini's staff at the Italy national team, though he made clear his intentions to become a head coach himself.
And Juve, who face Lecce on Sunday, would be Bonucci's dream role at club level.
"It is a project that began almost ten years ago. At 30, I had an idea of when my playing career would end and how much time I would need to earn my coaching badges," said Bonucci at an event.
"I am 39 now, and I had promised myself I would become a head coach at 40. Next year, I will complete the final qualification I need to coach at every level.

"But now I am on this journey with the national team, which is enjoyable, exciting and stressful. Perhaps I will put it off for a few years, but the goal is to try to become a head coach, because making it is far from guaranteed.
"Juventus [is the goal] above all. But I think there is a professional side to you that pushes you to accept challenges even when they go against your personal preferences.
"The desire to become a coach pushes you even further. But the dream is Juventus or the national team."
Following Juve's poor start under Luciano Spalletti, who is very much under pressure, they are just two points ahead of their upcoming opponents Lecce.
Lecce head into this contest with plenty of confidence after thrashing Udinese 3-0 last time out.
Lecce – Tiago Gabriel
Tiago Gabriel has scored four goals in Serie A since the start of last season, the most by any defender born in 2004 or later.
Among these players, he also leads in appearances (43), interceptions (54), clearances (274), and aerial duels won (138) in the competition over the same period.
Juventus – Randal Kolo Muani
Six of Randal Kolo Muani's nine Serie A goals for Juventus have been scored away from home (67%).

Among players who have netted at least as many goals for the club in the competition, only Sergio Brio (75%) has a higher percentage of away goals (Federico Chiesa, Michele Padovano and Riccardo Carapellese also have 67%).
MATCH PREDICTION: JUVENTUS WIN
This is the first time in Serie A history Lecce and Juve have faced each other from MD8 onwards with fewer than three points separating them.
Prior to this season, the smallest gap between the two sides after seven games was on MD17 of the 1989-90 campaign (four points in favour of Juve).
Only Inter (13) have won more Serie A away games against Lecce than Juve (12, level with Roma), while there have been five draws and three wins for Lecce.
Lecce have won just one of their 20 Serie A matches against Juve since the 2004-05 season (D5 L14): a 2-0 victory on 20th February 2011, with goals from Djamel Mesbah and Andrea Bertolacci.

Juventus have picked up 11 points so far in this Serie A season (W3 D2 L2); should they fail to win against Lecce, they would have fewer than 14 points after their first eight games in two consecutive seasons for the first time in the three-points-for-a-win era.
